turn_text: What about the river? You sponsored the Stop Sillage Overflow Act. So this is not a new issue for you. You've been doing conservation issues for a long time. What's next? What's next for the river in particular?

Yeah, so we are, I mean, every community along the Merrimack River knows just how serious combined sewage overflow is and how long it's taken for serious action to finally happen to address it. I mean, the numbers are just shocking, right? There's an average of 550 million gallons of raw sewage released into the Merrimack River every year. And sometimes that reaches, you know, dangerous levels on a day like when we have a lot of rain. And so we've been able to work on solutions at all levels of government with incredible partners. I mean, certainly in in Congress, I get to work with representatives Moulton and Chris Pappas from Manchester, Annie Custer from Nashua. But also with our Merrimack Valley State delegation. And it's clearly the organizations your outside groups like the Merrimack River Watershed Council and the Massachusetts River Alliance they've been unbelievable partners. We have to get the federal government to shift from loans or thinking about this in terms of loans to grants. And the federal government has done this. We have made investments in water infrastructure in the past. And the reality is the communities that are having the hardest trouble keeping up with the maintenance and with the upgrading of this infrastructure are the communities that can afford it the least. And so that is why we got legislation passed in the house as part of our infrastructure package last July. The Senate, sadly, like it did with so many of the bills, they did not move on it. But while we weren't able to get it across the finish line last year, we know that the Biden-Harris administration plans to make infrastructure a top priority this year. Given the bipartisan agreement that we already have, this is so necessary. So I'm confident that we're going to get combined sewerage overflow, our stop sewerage overflow act into the infrastructure package in the first half of this year.
